memory_update.text: VRT, ETN, GEV, PWR, and AAON are the top five candidates for this node in the current pass because each maps directly to power/cooling/grid/site-delivery constraints and has recent evidence tied to data-center or AI infrastructure demand.

POWL should remain on the watchlist as a less obvious, more specialized medium-voltage switchgear and packaged power-systems candidate; it was not included in the top-five list only because the pass was capped at five candidates.

MOD and NVT should be tracked in the cooling/liquid-cooling sub-bucket as second-wave candidates; both appear relevant, but need deeper revenue-share and customer-concentration validation before ranking above the broader infrastructure leaders.

The node appears to split into four investable sub-buckets: critical data-center power/cooling systems, electrical gear and transformers, grid/power-generation equipment, and engineering/construction labor for interconnection and site delivery.

This pass did not fully cover data-center REITs, utilities with specific hyperscaler power contracts, private transformer suppliers, non-US-listed leaders such as Schneider Electric/ABB/Siemens Energy, or land/site developers. These require separate node-specific passes.

node: Data-center power, cooling, grid interconnection, and site delivery
summary: Expanded universe for the AI data-center physical-infrastructure chokepoint. The highest-relevance US-listed candidates cluster around critical power/cooling systems, electrical gear, grid/power generation equipment, engineering/construction labor, and specialized data-center cooling. This pass prioritizes companies with observable backlog/order evidence or explicit company disclosures tying demand to data centers, AI capacity growth, or grid/electrification constraints. No buy/sell view is implied.
